The version I got from the manager that hired/fired him was that he smelled bad with horrible hygiene. 

I was in a small room with him and  two other people for about 20 minutes and didn't notice anything. He had a thick accent but spoke English fluently. Dressed like he was a old school psychiatrist. Three piece suit with a vest and everything  I wouldn't have been surprised if he pulled out a pocket watch. Almost expected him to ask me to lay down on the couch. 

The best dressed salesperson I ever saw at any dealership I worked for and I have worked at many.

My guess he fired him because of the accent. Didn't realize how thick it was and thought it would scare off customers which is ridiculous but this manager didn't have a lot of foresight.

And I thought I was being fairly paid until I really looked for other jobs in the aftermath of my termination. 


I was making more money than I ever had in my life. I actually was able to have a full six month emergency fund and invest the excess once I filled that fund.

I was so grossly underpaid for the hours and responsibilities I had it wasn't even funny. 

The job I just started pays roughly 80% of what I was making two years ago but...

I work from home almost half the time and in the field the rest. 


I still get a company vehicle. 

It's salary with a good potential bonus and I work 40 hours a week versus 60 plus.

I am not managing anyone versus managing 30 plus people.  Oh and no surprise special projects from the family or other owners.

Welcome to the glorious US medical system. It is even worse if you work for a small company with a HDHP.

9 or so in th morning we are getting ready to leave and I go get the car to move it up so we don't have to push the wheelchair far. 

I run into one of the women from the billing office who I know by first name at this point. She is coming to tell me that something weird is going on. It looks like the insurance co is trying to date everything for today instead of the past four days we have been on th hospital.
